handoff.purpose: Defines core dataclasses: Claim, TurnRef, ParticipantRecord, CouncilRecord with validation and a derived property.

symbols.name: Claim
symbols.note: Dataclass for one assertion by one participant. Fields: author, vendor, model, round, role, text, cites, checkable, check, verbatim, parsed. Docstring says checkable is true only when author supplied a concrete deterministic check.

symbols.name: TurnRef
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for one chained turn. Fields: turn_id, round, actor, vendor, model, role, status, reason, content, blind, self_review, duplicate_class, lane, withheld, latency_s.

symbols.name: ParticipantRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for roster accounting. Fields: actor, vendor, model, independence_class, lane, outcome, reason, withheld, rounds_spoken, operator_trusted.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for council output. Fields include council_id, question, evidence_label, evidence_digest, evidence_refs, rounds_requested, rounds_run, participants, turns, claims, requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, duplicate_classes, degraded, anomalies, floor_rule, ended, store_path, chain_head, chain_intact, chain_failures, tokens_charged, token_ceiling, wall_clock_s, advisory (always True). Has __post_init__ validation and property checkable_claims.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.checkable_claims
symbols.note: Property returning tuple of claims where c.checkable is True. Docstring: 'The queue the gate can actually run.'

claims.text: "checkable is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check -- a command, a test, a specific line assertion."
claims.why: The logic that sets checkable is not in this chunk; we only see the field default is False. The claim about when it is set to True cannot be verified here.

claims.text: "That is the council's entire product: a queue of checks for the gate to run."
claims.why: Refers to the gate and the product; not present in this chunk.

claims.text: "A claim without one is still recorded verbatim, and still counts for nothing on its own."
claims.why: The behavior of how claims are used is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "One chained turn, with the id it landed under and its content verbatim."
claims.why: TurnRef has turn_id and content fields to hold that information.
The class fields provide accounting (outcome, rounds_spoken, etc.).

claims.text: "The council's output. ADVISORY. It promotes nothing."
claims.why: The class has advisory=True by default and __post_init__ enforces it cannot be False.

claims.text: "There is deliberately no majority, no score, no consensus and no approve/reject field, and none may be added: a caller must not be able to destructure a decision out of this object."
claims.why: The fields listed in the class do not include majority, score, consensus, approve, or reject. The advisory field is always True.

claims.text: "What is here instead is every claim with its author and its evidence, the checkable subset, and honest roster accounting."
claims.why: Class has claims (tuple of Claim), checkable_claims property, and participants (tuple of ParticipantRecord).

claims.text: "Always True and enforced. This object is evidence, not a decision."
claims.why: Field default is True and __post_init__ raises ValueError if advisory is not True.

claims.text: "The queue the gate can actually run."
claims.why: The property returns only claims where checkable is True, which matches 'queue the gate can run'.

observations.what: END_REASONS is referenced in __post_init__ but not defined or imported in this chunk. It must be defined elsewhere in the file or imported.
DEFAULT_TOKEN_CEILING is used as default for token_ceiling but is not defined in this chunk. It must be defined elsewhere.

The docstring for Claim says 'checkable is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check'. The code does not enforce this; it only has a default False. The logic that sets checkable is not here.
CouncilRecord has many fields; the __post_init__ only validates advisory and ended. Other fields (e.g., chain_head, chain_intact) are not validated.

The docstring for TurnRef says 'One chained turn, with the id it landed under and its content verbatim.' The class has turn_id and content fields, but no indication of how chaining works. This is uncheckable.
